card.name: Next-word slots in label warnings
card.fires_on: Marked words in drug-label warning and lab sections, often the end of a medical word (opiates, preservatives, neutrophils, anemia) or a short verb such as 'was' or 'need' right after a medical noun.

modes.label: Ends of medical words
modes.description: The final piece of a longer clinical term, such as a blood cell, a test substance or an additive.
modes.example: Elevations of neutroph<<ils>> were not observed.

modes.label: Short words after a safety term
modes.description: A verb or noun right after a warning subject like mania, infections or addiction.
modes.example: During all MDD phase 2 and phase 3 studies, mania<< was>> reported for approximately 0.02

modes.label: Unit endings after a number
modes.description: The last piece of a unit or per-day phrase after a dose or count.
modes.example: (less than 1000/μ<<L>> for those with Benign Ethnic Neut

card.writes: Little clear effect; it weakly favors words about priority and a few Chinese terms, and suppresses odd name fragments.
card.plain: It fires on the closing piece of medical terms and on the word right after a warning topic in label text.
